page: Microsoft Azure FX24mds_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-dense virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with two threads per core, running at a sustained base frequency of 4.2 GHz. The hardware architecture incorporates a 260 MB L3 cache along with hardware-level support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. Memory capacity is substantial at 504 GB, resulting in a high allocation of 21 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance is not equipped with discrete GPU accelerators, but it includes 1416 GB of local NVMe SSD storage for scratch data and caching needs.

Benchmark data reflects exceptional single-thread capabilities attributable to the 4.2 GHz clock rate and large cache. Geekbench single-core testing reached 2367.0, placing it in the top ten percent of tested instances, with correspondingly top-tier metrics in image processing and text processing. Compression performance is similarly elevated, demonstrating 34.92 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and strong bzip3 decompression. Static web serving throughput measured 45.9 GB/sec. Across broader multi-threaded metrics, including stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and Redis SET throughput, results remain consistently in the median tier, highlighting that computational throughput is concentrated in per-core execution rather than horizontal core scale.

Resource allocation presents clear qualitative tradeoffs. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio and high clock speed deliver substantial compute capacity per thread without requiring an excessively high core count. This makes the FX24mds_v2 cost-effective for software licensed on a per-core basis that requires massive memory arrays. The integration of 1416 GB of local NVMe SSD provides fast local scratch space, though persistent storage architectures must account for its ephemeral nature. The instance is best suited for electronic design automation (EDA), large-footprint in-memory databases, batch data compilation, and simulation pipelines that demand high single-thread clock speeds.
description: Microsoft Azure FX24mds_v2 is a compute- and memory-intensive virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 24 dedicated vCPUs derived from 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, backed by a 260 MB L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX execution units. The server includes 504 GB of system memory (21 GB per vCPU) and 1416 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, without attached GPU accelerators. Benchmark results show top-tier single-core Geekbench performance alongside strong compression and static web serving speeds, while general multi-core stress tests and memory write throughput operate within median tiers. The pairing of elevated clock frequencies, massive per-core memory capacity, and fast local NVMe storage establishes strong efficiency for workloads with heavy single-thread demands and extreme memory footprints, such as electronic design automation (EDA), in-memory databases, simulation pipelines, and compilation tasks.
